title: Existence of a bounded Lipschitz probability kernel supported in the unit ball
statement: For every n ∈ ℕ there are ρ : ℝⁿ → ℝ (ℝⁿ = Euclid n) and C ∈ ℝ such that ρ is continuous, ρ ≥ 0, ρ(z) = 0 whenever ‖z‖ ≥ 1, ∫ρ = 1, |ρ(z)| ≤ C for all z, and |ρ(z) − ρ(z')| ≤ C‖z − z'‖ for all z, z'.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ), ∃ (ρ : Euclid n → ℝ) (C : ℝ), Continuous ρ ∧ (∀ z, 0 ≤ ρ z) ∧ (∀ z : Euclid n, 1 ≤ ‖z‖ → ρ z = 0) ∧ ∫ z, ρ z = 1 ∧ (∀ z, |ρ z| ≤ C) ∧ ∀ z z', |ρ z - ρ z'| ≤ C * ‖z - z'‖
